title: 2-Year Floating Rate Note auction (quarterly new issue) — sells on the FOMC decision day
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF, text layer decompressed direct 2026-09-05 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) — row reads `2-Year FRN / Announcement Thursday, October 22, 2026 / Auction Wednesday, October 28, 2026 / Settlement Monday, November 02, 2026`, and carries NO `R` marker while the 08-20, 09-17, 11-19 and 12-17 FRN rows in the same PDF all read `2-Year FRNR` — i.e. this is the quarterly new issue. Size corroborated in advance by press release sb0590 (2026-08-05), read as text direct 2026-09-05, whose Oct-26 anticipated-size row reads 30 in the FRN column (header `2-Year 3-Year 5-Year 7-Year 10-Year 20-Year 30-Year FRN`, row `69 58 70 44 39 13 22 30`); the auction record agrees independently, with 10 consecutive quarterly new issues at $30B since 2024-04-24 and 20 consecutive reopenings at $28B since 2024-05-29 (fiscaldata auctions_query, floating_rate:Yes, pulled 2026-09-05). Stays estimate on two counts: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2026-10-22 announcement itself. CORRECTION (2026-09-05, this event's initial research): the ~11:30 ET auction slot IS sourced after all — fiscaldata's auctions_query publishes `closing_time_comp`, which reads `11:30 AM` on 137 of the 154 FRN auctions since 2014, with every one of the 16 `01:00 PM` exceptions falling in a holiday or short week (Thanksgiving, late December) and 2026-10-28 being an ordinary Wednesday. The earlier note that the time was unsourced described where the discovering lane had looked, not the record
notes: The one security of the four sized by treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-10-22 that had no calendar row, while treasury-2y-note-2026-10-26, treasury-5y-note-2026-10-27 and treasury-7y-note-2026-10-29 all did — and the only one selling on an FOMC decision day (fomc-2026-10-28). That pairing LOOKS like supply into a policy event and is measured NOT to be: crossing all 69 FRN auctions from 2021-01-01 to 2026-09-04 against the Fed's own published decision dates, 9 sold on a decision day and 8 of the 9 were quarterly new issues (2021-01-27, 2021-07-28, 2022-01-26, 2022-07-27, 2023-07-26, 2025-10-29, 2026-01-28, 2026-07-29) — 8 of 23 new issues, ~35%, because Treasury's FRN new-issue slot sits in the last week of January/April/July/October and the FOMC's meetings end in that same week. The raw margin gap (high discount margin 7.05bp on-FOMC vs 13.17bp off) is composition, not effect; within-CUSIP controls remove the level and show nothing — DM(first reopening) minus DM(its own new issue) is +0.43bp on-FOMC vs +0.70bp off, and DM(new issue) minus DM(the immediately preceding auction) is -1.23bp on vs -0.70bp off. Mechanism claimed: an FRN indexed to the 13-week bill resets weekly and absorbs the decision. Live context: the discount margin is at a FOUR-YEAR LOW — 5.0bp on 2026-07-29 and 5.5bp on 2026-08-26, the last sub-5.0bp print being 2022-07-27 — with a named but unmeasured mechanism, sb0590's own 'SOMA purchases of Treasury bills and growing demand for Treasury bills from the private sector'. The one FRN auction between now and this one is the 2026-09-23 reopening, which is the free read on whether that low is a level or a moment. Read-it-do-not-trade-it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed. This event does NOT re-register the FOMC-CONCESSION prediction: FT-treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-10-22-2 already owns that and scores 2026-10-29 — inherit it rather than duplicating one observation. Discovered during the treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-10-22 initial research (2026-09-05), which found this calendar had never recorded a floating-rate note or a discount margin at all. THE FOUR-YEAR LOW IS NOW MEASURED, by this event's own initial research (2026-09-05): the discount margin is MOSTLY A CURVE-SLOPE READOUT, not a scarcity readout. Regressing high_discnt_margin on the 2Y-3M par-curve slope of each auction's own date (all 69 auctions since 2021, every one matched to Treasury's daily par-curve CSV) gives R2 0.758 and beta -10.08bp per 100bp of slope; on 2022+ (n=57, excluding the badly-fitting ZIRP regime) R2 0.790. The slope swung -45bp (2025-09) to +46bp (2026-09-04), which at that beta accounts for roughly 10bp of the ~15bp compression, and the tail agrees — 2022-04-27 sold at a +191bp slope and printed a NEGATIVE -7.5bp margin against a fitted -8.9bp. The bill-demand channel is what is left over and it is SMALL: a model trained only on 2023-2025 and run out-of-sample on 2026 under-predicts by mean -2.19bp, 6 of 8 errors negative, -3.89 and -3.79 on the two most recent prints — so 2-4bp, not 15bp. Demand composition REFUTES the intuitive reading that the low margin is investors fighting for paper: 2026 indirect share 61.3% is BELOW 2024's 66.5% when margins ran 15-19bp, direct has collapsed to 0.2% (four 2026 auctions took zero), bid-to-cover 3.18 sits inside its 2021-2025 range, and corr(DM, bid-to-cover) is only -0.21 — grade a print on composition, never on level. SECOND MEASURED RESULT, A CLEAN NULL: the FRN auction session does nothing to the tape (ex-FOMC, n=40 since 2023, vs 920 sessions — 3M CMT +0.05bp t=+0.40, 2Y +0.70bp t=+1.07, 10Y +0.25bp t=+0.13), and the tempting 'auction days are quieter' version FAILS ITS CONTROL: 35 of 44 FRN auctions are Wednesdays, and the |2Y move| gap collapses from t=-4.19 vs all sessions to t=-2.16 vs Wednesdays alone (3M -4.71 to -1.55). Recorded as no FRN-specific tape effect detected, which is the OPPOSITE of treasury-2y-note-2026-10-26's measured -4.70bp at t=-4.60 — a note auction transfers duration, a floater auction does not. This event registers ONE test of its own, FT-treasury-2y-frn-2026-10-28-1, scored five weeks early on the 2026-09-23 reopening (proposed as its own calendar file treasury-2y-frn-2026-09-23 in the same PR): the margin lands within +/-3.0bp of `DM_bp = 10.43 - 11.02 x slope_pp`, point estimate 5.4bp at the +46bp slope. DATA TRAPS, NAMED: fiscaldata's high_discnt_margin is in PERCENT (0.049000 = 4.9bp), and security_term reads `2-Year` on new issues but `1-Year 11-Month` / `1-Year 10-Month` on reopenings, so filtering on `2-Year` silently drops all 46 reopenings.
